identity.creator: DeepSeek (Hangzhou DeepSeek Artificial Intelligence Co., Ltd.)
identity.model_family: DeepSeek-R1 (distilled into Qwen2.5 and Llama 3 base architectures)

architecture.active_parameters: All variants are dense models, so active parameters equal total parameters: 1.5B, 7B, 8B, 14B, 32B, 70B respectively.
architecture.architecture_type: Dense transformer. Not MoE. The Qwen-based variants (1.5B, 7B, 14B, 32B) use the Qwen2.5 dense transformer architecture. The Llama-based variants (8B, 70B) use the Llama 3.1/3.3 dense transformer architecture.
architecture.context_window: 128K tokens (inherited from base architectures). Practical context usage may vary by deployment platform and available memory.
architecture.max_output_tokens: Up to 32,768 tokens (including chain-of-thought reasoning and final answer). Some deployment platforms cap at 16K. Recommended to keep under 8,192 for optimal quality.

capabilities.open_or_closed: Open-weight (downloadable weights on Hugging Face). Training code partially available. Distillation training data (800K samples) not publicly released.
capabilities.license_type: Varies by base model. Qwen-based distills (1.5B, 7B, 14B, 32B): Apache 2.0 (inherited from Qwen2.5). Llama-based distills (8B, 70B): MIT License. All variants explicitly support commercial use, modifications, and derivative works including further distillation. No restrictive clauses.
capabilities.reasoning_capability: Fixed chain-of-thought reasoning. The models were fine-tuned on 800,000 reasoning samples generated by the full DeepSeek-R1 model, inheriting its step-by-step reasoning behavior. They produce a <think>...</think> block containing chain-of-thought before the final answer. Reasoning cannot be toggled off or budget-controlled. Unlike the full R1, these distilled models use only supervised fine-tuning (SFT) without a reinforcement learning stage. The 32B variant outperforms OpenAI o1-mini on reasoning benchmarks.
capabilities.multimodal_support: Text only. No image, audio, or video input/output. No code execution or web browsing built in. Purely text-in, text-out models.
capabilities.multilingual_support: Primarily optimized for English and Chinese. The base Qwen2.5 architecture supports broader multilingual coverage than the Llama-based variants. French is supported but not a primary language; the model may produce reasoning chains in English or Chinese even when prompted in French. Community fine-tuned multilingual variants exist (e.g., lightblue/DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-7B-Multilingual) that improve non-English chain-of-thought consistency. [uncertain]
capabilities.agentic_capability: Limited native agentic capability. The distilled models do not natively support function calling or tool use. However, their strong coding abilities allow them to produce actions as Python code for agentic workflows through code-based interaction patterns. The full DeepSeek-R1 surpasses Claude 3.5 Sonnet by 12.5% on GAIA agentic benchmarks using code-action approaches, but the distilled models have reduced capability here. Community solutions (e.g., MFDoom/deepseek-r1-tool-calling on Ollama) add tool-calling support via prompt engineering. Later DeepSeek models (V3.1) significantly improved tool use over the R1 family.

benchmarks.key_benchmarks: DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-32B: AIME 2024: 72.6%, MATH-500: 94.3%, GPQA Diamond: 62.1%, LiveCodeBench: 57.2%, Codeforces: 1691. DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-14B: AIME 2024: 69.7%, MATH-500: 93.9%, GPQA Diamond: 59.1%, Codeforces: 1481. DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-7B: AIME 2024: 55.5%, MATH-500: 92.8%, GPQA Diamond: 49.1%, Codeforces: 1189. DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-1.5B: AIME 2024: 28.9%, MATH-500: 83.9%, Codeforces: 954. DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Llama-70B: AIME 2024: 70.0%, MATH-500: 94.5%, GPQA Diamond: 65.2%, Codeforces: 1633. DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Llama-8B: AIME 2024: 50.4%, MATH-500: 89.1%, GPQA Diamond: 49.0%, Codeforces: 1205. For reference, OpenAI o1-mini scores: AIME 2024: 63.6%, MATH-500: 90.0%, GPQA Diamond: 60.0%, Codeforces: 1820.
benchmarks.reasoning_benchmarks_composite: The 32B Qwen variant is the standout: AIME 2024 72.6% vs o1-mini 63.6%, MATH-500 94.3% vs o1-mini 90.0%, GPQA Diamond 62.1% vs o1-mini 60.0%. The 32B variant outperforms o1-mini on math and science reasoning while being fully open-weight. The 70B Llama variant achieves the highest MATH-500 score (94.5%) among all distilled models. Even the 7B model (MATH-500: 92.8%) surpasses o1-mini on math benchmarks. The 14B variant (AIME 2024: 69.7%) also beats o1-mini on competition math.

pricing.pricing_per_1M_tokens: The distilled models are open-weight and free to download and self-host. For API access via DeepSeek's platform (full R1, not distilled specifically): $0.56 input (cache miss) / $0.07 input (cache hit) / $1.68 output per 1M tokens (as of September 2025). Third-party providers offer the distilled models at varying prices: Together AI, Groq, Fireworks, NVIDIA NIM, and others host specific distilled variants, often at lower cost than the full R1. Self-hosting eliminates per-token costs entirely.
pricing.cost_efficiency_notes: The distilled models represent perhaps the most cost-efficient reasoning models available. Self-hosting the 14B or 32B variant on a single consumer GPU (RTX 4090) delivers reasoning performance that rivals or exceeds OpenAI o1-mini at zero marginal token cost. The 7B variant can run on GPUs as small as 8GB VRAM with 4-bit quantization. Even through third-party APIs, the distilled variants are dramatically cheaper than proprietary reasoning models. DeepSeek's own API pricing ($0.56/$1.68 per 1M tokens) is already 5-20x cheaper than OpenAI o1/o3. The open-weight nature means no vendor lock-in and full control over inference costs.

deployment.minimum_hardware_requirement: Varies by model size. FP16 (full precision): 1.5B ~3GB VRAM, 7B ~14GB VRAM, 8B ~16GB VRAM, 14B ~26GB VRAM, 32B ~60-65GB VRAM, 70B ~140GB VRAM. With 4-bit quantization (Q4_K_M): 1.5B ~1.2GB (runs on CPU), 7B ~4-6GB, 8B ~5-7GB, 14B ~9GB, 32B ~18-20GB (fits RTX 4090), 70B ~40GB (needs 2x RTX 4090 or A100). The 1.5B model can run on phones and laptops with CPU-only inference. The 7B model fits comfortably on consumer GPUs like RTX 3060 12GB with quantization.
deployment.quantization_availability: Extensive quantization support across all formats. GGUF: available for all variants via community uploads (Unsloth, bartowski, Mungert on Hugging Face), supporting Q2_K through Q8_0. GPTQ: available. AWQ: available. ONNX: official Microsoft/ONNX Runtime optimized versions for CPU, GPU, and NPU. INT4 per-channel quantization with INT16 activations (QuaRot scheme) for NPU deployment. bitsandbytes: supported through Hugging Face Transformers integration.
deployment.on_device_capable: Yes, strongly on-device capable. The 1.5B variant is specifically optimized for on-device deployment: runs on Copilot+ PCs via Windows Copilot Runtime (Qualcomm Snapdragon X NPU, Intel Core Ultra 200V NPU), achieves <70ms time to first token and ~40 tokens/s on NPU, runs on Android phones via Termux/llama.cpp, runs on iPhones via MLX. The 7B and 8B variants run on high-end laptops with discrete GPUs. Microsoft includes NPU-optimized versions in the Azure AI Model Catalog. ONNX Runtime optimized versions published for cross-platform on-device inference.

business.best_use_cases: 1) Cost-free reasoning for startups: self-host the 14B or 32B model to get o1-mini-level reasoning at zero per-query cost, ideal for math tutoring, financial analysis, and technical problem-solving products. 2) On-device AI applications: deploy the 1.5B model on phones and laptops for offline reasoning-capable assistants, privacy-preserving AI, and edge computing scenarios where data cannot leave the device. 3) Custom fine-tuning base: use the distilled models as starting points for domain-specific reasoning models (legal reasoning, medical diagnosis support, engineering calculations) since the open license permits unlimited modification. 4) Coding assistance and code review: the strong LiveCodeBench and Codeforces scores make the 32B and 70B variants effective for developer tools, automated code review, and technical documentation generation. 5) Education and training platforms: build interactive math and science tutoring systems that can explain step-by-step reasoning, leveraging the visible chain-of-thought output.
business.relevance_for_entrepreneurs: The DeepSeek-R1 distilled models are a watershed moment for startup AI accessibility. For the first time, reasoning capabilities that rival OpenAI's paid API (o1-mini) are available as fully open-weight models that can run on a single consumer GPU. Key business implications: (1) Eliminates API dependency — no per-query costs, no rate limits, no vendor lock-in. A startup can serve millions of reasoning queries from a single rented GPU server at fixed infrastructure cost. (2) Enables privacy-first products — the models run entirely on-premise or on-device, critical for European startups navigating GDPR or handling sensitive data (health, legal, financial). (3) The permissive licenses (Apache 2.0 / MIT) allow unlimited commercial use without licensing fees, even for further distillation into proprietary models. (4) Dramatically lowers the barrier for AI-native products: a 2-person startup can embed frontier-class reasoning into their product without negotiating enterprise API contracts. (5) The 1.5B model running on phones opens entirely new product categories: offline AI tutors, on-device financial calculators, privacy-preserving personal assistants. The trade-off: no multimodal support, limited tool use, and weaker multilingual performance compared to proprietary alternatives. For European entrepreneurs, the open-weight nature sidesteps concerns about data being sent to Chinese or US servers.
business.competitive_position: The DeepSeek-R1 distilled models occupy a unique position as the first open-weight reasoning models to match or exceed a proprietary reasoning model (o1-mini). The 32B variant is the sweet spot: outperforms o1-mini on AIME 2024 (72.6% vs 63.6%) and MATH-500 (94.3% vs 90.0%) while being fully self-hostable. Key competitors: Qwen2.5 (strong base but without R1-level reasoning), Phi-4 14B (competitive on math/coding but Microsoft-controlled), Llama 3.3 70B (strong general capability but without dedicated reasoning training). Weaknesses: text-only (no multimodal), limited native tool use, reasoning chains can be excessively long, French/multilingual support is secondary, and the models may mix Chinese into outputs. The later DeepSeek-R1-0528 update improved reasoning further but did not release new distilled variants at launch.
business.ecosystem_and_tooling: Exceptionally broad ecosystem support. Local inference: Ollama (first-class support with multiple quantization tags), LM Studio, llama.cpp, Jan.ai. Serving frameworks: vLLM, TGI (Text Generation Inference), SGLang, TensorRT-LLM. Cloud APIs: Together AI, Groq, Fireworks AI, NVIDIA NIM, DeepInfra, Replicate, AWS Bedrock, Azure AI Foundry. Frameworks: Hugging Face Transformers, LangChain, LlamaIndex. On-device: ONNX Runtime, Windows Copilot Runtime (NPU), Apple MLX. Quantization providers: Unsloth (GGUF), bartowski (GGUF), TheBloke community. IDE integrations: compatible with any OpenAI-API-compatible coding assistant (Continue, Aider, Open Interpreter) when self-hosted.
business.geographic_origin_and_regulation: China (Hangzhou, Zhejiang Province). DeepSeek has faced significant regulatory scrutiny in Europe: Italy's Garante ordered DeepSeek to block Italian access to its R1 app/API over GDPR violations, investigations launched in 13 European jurisdictions, and the European Data Protection Board created a dedicated AI Enforcement Task Force. HOWEVER, these concerns primarily apply to DeepSeek's hosted API and app, NOT to the open-weight models. When self-hosted by a European company, the distilled models avoid data sovereignty issues entirely — no data is sent to Chinese servers. This is a critical distinction for European entrepreneurs: downloading and self-hosting the Apache 2.0 / MIT licensed weights is legally unproblematic under GDPR and the EU AI Act, while using DeepSeek's hosted API raises the same data transfer concerns as any non-EU cloud provider. For EU AI Act compliance, deployers of the open-weight models would be responsible for their own compliance as 'deployers' rather than relying on DeepSeek as a 'provider'.
